key_catalyst: TSMC's raised $60-64B capex triggering a sector-wide semiconductor and memory-chip selloff as the market sold strong earnings on valuation/duration fears
reasoning: Today's -1.07% decline was driven by a valuation-compression regime shift: the market inverted the normal reaction and sold TSMC's record earnings and $60-64B capex hike, cascading into a brutal memory-chip collapse (Micron -8%, SK Hynix -9%, SanDisk -8.1%) while the 10-year yield ripped to 4.60% just shy of the 4.62% cycle high after 208K jobless claims snapped the rate-cut narrative. Unlike the 07-13 geopolitical shock that fully rebounded on 07-14's cool CPI, this is a multi-catalyst de-rating with yields near cycle highs and Asia already contaging (KOSPI -6.4% overnight), and only Apple's idiosyncratic all-time high cushioned the tape. The confluence of rising discount rates, an unwinding storage supercycle, and Hormuz escalation leaves material overnight gap-down risk rather than a single absorbed shock.
